chapter_note: A remarkably clean teaching chapter dominated by substrate cosmological process description. The chapter describes the three-fold discharge cycle: the Father of Life pours dark vessels (water, darkness, fire) onto earth, the corresponding dark elements in the earths are drawn upward by sympathetic attraction ('like draws like'), then both are swept into prepared pits. The systematic parallel structure across paragraphs 9-11 (water, then darkness, then fire) is classic substrate enumeration. No editorial bridge, institutional, or exhortation material detected. The only later material is dialogue frame formulas in paragraphs 1, 2, 7, 8. The term 'Father of Life' for the demiurge (rather than 'Living Spirit') may preserve an earlier stratum as Gardner notes. The negative editorial fatigue score confirms the chapter stays consistently substratic throughout.

paragraphs.core_text: When the Father of Life discharged these three vessels from above, they of water and of darkness and of fire, did he perhaps discharge them to their pits at the edge of the firmament? Or did he discharge them first to this earth, and then he swept them from the earth and threw them to their places?
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame formula: 'Once again the disciples questioned him, saying to him:'
paragraphs.temporal_note: The question is fully substantive — it defines the teaching structure by posing the exact cosmological process question (direct discharge vs. pour-then-sweep). This is the Persian pedagogical question format defining the topic.

paragraphs.core_text: when the Father of Life was about to discharge these three vessels he poured the three upon this earth, one by one at its (appointed) hour and season. He discharged them and cast them down to the earth.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame attribution and transitional phrasing: 'Then the apostle says to them: As for what you have asked me about the vessels, you must understand this, that'
paragraphs.temporal_note: The frame formula 'Then the apostle says to them' and the pedagogical transition 'As for what you have asked me... you must understand this, that' are editorial. The teaching content describes the sequential discharge process with temporal ordering ('one by one at its appointed hour and season').

paragraphs.core_text: Then he bailed and scooped them from this earth in these three garments, they of wind and of water and of fire, which swathed his body. He poured and made them flow into the three pits [ ... w]hich he had [es]tablished during the construc[tio]n of the worlds [ ... ] they [ ... ] something remained behind on the face of the earth from these three vessels, so that you can find their mark and type displayed in the universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure cosmological process. The three light garments (wind, water, fire) correspond to the three dark vessels — a systematic pairing. 'Mark and type displayed in the universe' is correspondential language: the remnants of cosmic process leave visible traces in the physical world. Both sides of the mapping stay within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: The element that is left in water is the pungency and the salinity of this salty inner sea that surrounds the worlds.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First of three remnant-correspondences. Maps residual dark water → sensory quality (pungency, salinity) → cosmic geography (inner sea surrounding worlds). Classic substrate: domain mapped onto domain, both sides within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: And the remnant that is left from the darkness is this black mountain that exists in the surroundings of the sunrise. For when the sun would shine over the world no sunlight is visible there, because the darkness that gushes from it manifests above it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second remnant-correspondence. Maps residual darkness → cosmic geography (black mountain near sunrise) → cosmological effect (blocks sunlight). Both sides internal to the cosmic system. The 'black mountain at sunrise' is cosmic geography, not a reference to any earthly location.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.118⟩
And the remnant that remains behind from the fire, upon the earth, are all the mountains and islands from where fumes of fire gush up and are visible. For these things are the remnant of the great vessel, the vestige that was conjoined with this fire that comes up from the earth; together with the mountains and hills [ ... ] places where no fruit sprouts on the trees [ ... ] greater than that place from the limb and [ ... / ... ] the trees shall not bear fruit in that place.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third remnant-correspondence. Maps residual fire → cosmic geography (volcanic mountains, barren islands) → effects (fumes, barrenness). Significant lacunae in the second half. The page marker ⟨p.118⟩ suggests manuscript disruption. Both sides of mapping remain within the cosmic system — volcanic phenomena as traces of the cosmic fire vessel.

paragraphs.core_text: about the vessels that surround the universe, and why they were not discharged from above into the ditches prepared for them (straightaway); but were firstly poured upon the earth, and afterwards were swept from the earth and cast down into their pits?
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame formula and honorific address: 'Once again his disciples speak to him: We ask you, our master, to [make clear] and instruct us'
paragraphs.temporal_note: The substantive question defines the second teaching sequence — it asks WHY the indirect discharge method was used. This is the structural question that the paragraphs 8-12 answer. The frame formula and honorific address ('our master') are editorial.

paragraphs.core_text: When the Father of Life discharged these vessels from above upon the earth, he poured them out for this reason: so that also the water and the darkness and the fire that exist in these three earths would be drawn and ascend towards they that had come down from above, and the earths would be purified and cleansed. Due to this he poured these vessels down to the earth, of water and of darkness and of fire, so that also the water and darkness and fire that exist in the earths would be drawn up towards they that had descended from above.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame attribution and pedagogical interjection: 'Then the enlightener speaks to his disciples: Happen you know this!'
paragraphs.temporal_note: The teaching describes the sympathetic attraction principle — like draws like across cosmic levels. Dark water from above draws dark water from below; dark fire draws dark fire. This is the core cosmological mechanism: discharge-attraction-purification. The repetitive phrasing (water/darkness/fire repeated twice) suggests oral-formulaic teaching structure.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.113⟩
Now, first of all, he discharged the water, the waste, the poison of the rulers who are above. He cleansed the firmaments of the [water ... ] he poured down the dark waters. [Just as the] waters fell from heaven to earth, so also the waters below in the earths were drawn and came up from below towards the waters that had come from above to the earths. The waters [were] purified of the dark poison that exists in them. Then he swept them outside and made them a great vessel and a wall of sea that surrounds the universe, and on which the ships sail.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First of three parallel discharge-purification sequences (water → darkness → fire). Describes the complete cycle: discharge from firmaments, sympathetic attraction of dark waters from the earths, purification, and formation into cosmic geography (wall of sea surrounding the universe). 'Poison of the rulers' is cosmic-agent vocabulary. 'Ships sail' refers to cosmic vessels (sun/moon ships) traversing the purified sea.

paragraphs.core_text: After the water, he discharged the darkness. He purified the firmaments and dried from them the darkness with which they are weighed down. He discharged it down to the earth. Just as he had purified the firmaments, so also he purified the earths. The darkness that is in the earths was drawn up towards the darkness that had been discharged from above. He swept them both out and shut them in that [ ... ] of darkness [ ... / ... ] the water.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second parallel discharge-purification sequence: darkness. Same structure as paragraph 9. The sympathetic attraction principle operates identically: darkness from below is drawn toward darkness discharged from above. Lacunae in the final portion obscure where exactly the darkness is confined.

paragraphs.core_text: And he discharged the fire from heaven to earth, [ ... at] that time again the fire that was shut [in] the earth below was drawn and came up towards its kind. Fire was added to fire. Afterwards, he swept it out and cast it into the outer underworld, which [he had constructed for] them outside the universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third parallel discharge-purification sequence: fire. 'Drawn and came up towards its kind' — the sympathetic attraction formula stated most concisely. 'Fire was added to fire' is the simplest expression of the like-draws-like principle. The fire is cast into the 'outer underworld' — cosmic geography. The three-fold parallel (water/darkness/fire) across paragraphs 9-11 is classic substrate enumeration structure.

paragraphs.core_text: In the same way that he purified the firmaments above as a place for the light-givers to journey [ ... / ... ] so also he purified the earths below and swept from them the fire and the darkness and the water [ ... ] He has purified them for the ascent of these three powers, they of the wind and the water and the fire, which ascend before the Porter and traverse the earths.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summary and purpose statement for the entire process. The purification creates pathways: above for the light-givers (sun, moon), below for the three light powers (wind, water, fire). 'The Porter' is a cosmic figure (one of the sons of the Living Spirit in Manichaean cosmology). Both sides of the mapping stay within the cosmic system: purified zones → pathways for cosmic beings. The light triad (wind, water, fire) mirrors the dark triad (water, darkness, fire) that was discharged.
